title: 1 · Sounds, spelling and stress
blurb: Read Portuguese words aloud the Brazilian way: nasal vowels, the letters that differ from English, and where the stress goes.

title: 2 · Greetings: ‹você› and ‹o senhor›
blurb: Greet people at any time of day, say thank you the right way, and choose between ‹você› and ‹o senhor›.

title: 3 · Gender and ‹o› / ‹a›, ‹um› / ‹uma›
blurb: Use the right 'the' and 'a' with any noun, make nouns plural, and order food with ‹um› and ‹uma›.

title: 4 · Subject pronouns and ‹ser›
blurb: Say who you are, where you're from and what you do, with every subject pronoun and the verb ‹ser›.

title: 5 · Adjectives: agreement and position
blurb: Describe people and things with adjectives that agree and sit in the right place.

title: 6 · Present tense: ‹-ar›, ‹-er›, ‹-ir›
blurb: Say what you and others do every day, with the right verb ending for each subject.

title: 7 · ‹estar›: where and how
blurb: Say where people and things are, how someone is right now, and ask where a place is with ‹ficar›.

title: 8 · ‹no›, ‹na›, ‹do›, ‹da›: contractions
blurb: Join ‹em› and ‹de› with ‹o› and ‹a›, and say where you are and where you're from with countries and cities.

title: 9 · ‹ser› vs ‹estar› (and ‹ficar›)
blurb: Choose between ‹ser›, ‹estar› and ‹ficar› by asking what you are describing.

title: 10 · ‹ter›: have, there is, and ‹estar com›
blurb: Say what you have, how old you are, what there is nearby, and that you're hungry, thirsty or cold.

title: 11 · Question words
blurb: Ask yes/no questions without any do, and ask who, what, where, when, how, how many and why.

title: 12 · Numbers, time and prices
blurb: Count to 1,000, tell the time, and read prices in ‹reais›.

title: 13 · Places and location words
blurb: Say where things are: near, far, on, under, next to, in front of, behind and inside.

title: 14 · ‹meu› / ‹minha›, ‹este› / ‹esse›
blurb: Say my, your, his, her and our, and point at things with this and that.

title: 15 · ‹ir›, ‹fazer›, ‹querer›, ‹poder›
blurb: Use four everyday irregular verbs to say where you're going, what you do, what you want and what you can do.

title: 16 · ‹ir› + infinitive: plans
blurb: Talk about plans and the future with ‹vou›, ‹vai›, ‹vamos› and ‹vão› plus a verb.

title: 17 · ‹gostar de›: likes
blurb: Say what you and others like and love, and agree with me too and me neither.

title: 18 · Prepositions: ‹de›, ‹em›, ‹para›, ‹por›, ‹com›
blurb: Use ‹para›, ‹por›, ‹com› and ‹de› the Brazilian way: where to, thanks for, with me, by bus.

title: 19 · ‹estar› + ‹-ndo›: right now
blurb: Say what is happening right now with ‹estar› + the ‹-ndo› form.

title: 20 · Reflexive verbs and daily routine
blurb: Say your name and describe your daily routine with ‹me›, ‹se› and ‹nos›.

title: 21 · Object pronouns: ‹me›, ‹te›, ‹ele›, ‹a gente›
blurb: Say 'help me', 'I love you' and 'I know him' the way Brazilians do.

title: 22 · ‹Pretérito perfeito›: what you did
blurb: Tell what you did yesterday or last weekend with the ‹pretérito perfeito›.

title: 23 · Polite requests and commands
blurb: Ask for help and order politely, and understand the commands you hear.

title: 24 · ‹e›, ‹mas›, ‹ou›, ‹porque›
blurb: Join sentences with ‹e›, ‹mas›, ‹ou›, ‹porque›, ‹então› and ‹quando›.

title: 25 · Getting around the city
blurb: Ask the way, follow directions, and get around by bus, metro or Uber.
